auth_bypass.instructions: code lets a request reach protected data or actions without the team's auth check

criteria.true: A route that returns or changes user data with no @require_auth, or a debug flag, header or parameter that skips the check
criteria.false: Public endpoints (health, login, static pages), routes that keep the auth check, or code that is not a request handler

sensitive_exposure.instructions: code sends secrets or personal data to logs, error messages or API responses

criteria.true: Passwords, tokens, hashes, emails or card data in logs, error messages or API responses
criteria.false: Masked or truncated values, booleans or counts about them, sending data to the place it belongs, or a credential written in source (that is hardcoded_secret)

layering.instructions: route or controller code talks to the database directly instead of through the repository layer

criteria.true: A file under routes/ or api/ that runs queries, sessions, cursors or ORM managers
criteria.false: Routes that call a repository or service, or database code inside repositories/

hardcoded_secret.instructions: code contains a real credential as a literal

criteria.true: A working-looking key, token, password or connection string with a password, in source
criteria.false: Values read from the environment or a secret manager, obvious test placeholders in tests/, or example values in docs

system:

Does not: Masked or truncated values, booleans or counts about them, sending data to the place it belongs, or a credential written in source (that is hardcoded_secret).
- layering: route or controller code talks to the database directly instead of through the repository layer. Breaks it: A file under routes/ or api/ that runs queries, sessions, cursors or ORM managers. Does not: Routes that call a repository or service, or database code inside repositories/.
- hardcoded_secret: code contains a real credential as a literal. Breaks it: A working-looking key, token, password or connection string with a password, in source. Does not: Values read from the environment or a secret manager, obvious test placeholders in tests/, or example values in docs.
